1. Two-electrode, symmetric pouch cell device assembly: 
 
For practical device performance, symmetric pouch cells were fabricated using TFS-
AC and TFS-AC(KOH) as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. The electrodes 
were prepared using the same slurry-casting  method as in the three-electrode setup, 
coated onto nickel foam substrates, and dried at 100 °C. A symmetric conﬁguration was 
constructed by sandwiching two iden tical electrodes with a Whatman ﬁlter paper 
separator soaked in 3 M KOH electrolyte. The components were assembled into a 
ﬂexible pouch-type casing to form a compact symmetric device. Electrochemical testing 
was conducted in a voltage window of 0 to 1.0 V. Performance analysis included CV, 
GCD and EIS studies to investigate the capacitance behavior, rate performance and 
internal resistance of the full device. This  setup allowed evaluation of the real-world 
supercapacitor performance and cycling durability of the bio-derived activated carbon 
materials.  
Both active materials, TFS-AC and TFS-AC (KOH), were coated onto pre-cleaned nickel 
foam substrates with an active material ma ss loading of approximately   ~1.6–2.8 mg 
per electrode. After oven drying, the mass  loading was determined by measuring the

electrode weight before and after coating. The electrode composition consisted of 80 
wt% active material (TFS-AC or TFS-AC (KOH)), 10 wt% conductive carbon, and 10 
wt% poly(vinylidene ﬂuoride) (PVDF) binder. The conductive carbon and PVDF binder 
contributed negligible mass to the electroc hemical performance calculations. Based on 
the measured active material mass, the corresponding speci ﬁc current was applied in 
the electrochemical workstation software. The speci ﬁc capacitance and other 
supercapacitor performance parameters were  calculated using the following equation 
(Equation S1).
